iut_type: Registration database DN display behavior for 'Combine unmodified Designs' (old Declaration-equivalent) registrations, and the SoC End Product vs. Subsystem-combination distinction for DN eligibility
customer_question: If we register by directly reusing an existing design ('Combine unmodified Designs') without a Design Number being assigned, does showing 'Default'/'Details' in the DN field cause any downsides or problems? Is it OK for Bluetooth certification purposes to re-brand using only a QDID starting with 'Q30'?
question_variants: How does a registration combining multiple existing QDID/DNs actually display in the SIG database search results?
Does a registration always fail to get a DN when reusing an existing design unmodified?
actual_issue: After trialing a 'reuse existing design unmodified' registration, the customer noticed the Receipt Number showed a warning icon and the DN field appeared as 'Default'/'Details' rather than a normal-looking Design Number, and asked whether this indicated a problem or limitation.
plain_english_explanation: For a short period after the new registration site launched on July 1, 2024, any registration equivalent to the old Declaration registration (Including an existing QDID/DN without editing its ICS) uniformly displayed 'Details' in the DN field, showing only the Included QDID/DN alongside it -- giving the visual impression that no DN was assigned at all. The site's behavior has since changed: if only one QDID/DN is Included, the display remains as before (no DN assigned), but if two or more QDID/DNs are Included together, the site now assigns a genuine Design Number -- prefixed with 'Q30' (denoting QPRDv3.0, the post-July-2024 registration framework) -- to the combined ICS of those Included designs, and displays it alongside the Included QDID/DNs (visible by following the 'Details' link/icon to the detail page). This Q30-prefixed DN carries exactly the same legal/certification effect as a pre-2024-style QDID, and other companies can Include it in their own downstream product registrations for test-exemption purposes, just as they could with an older QDID. One important related rule: this DN-assignment behavior specifically applies to registrations that combine multiple subsystem-level QDIDs (e.g., Controller Subsystem + Host Subsystem); if the SoC is instead registered directly as a complete End Product, no DN is assigned at all. Module sellers supplying components to downstream set-makers should therefore deliberately choose an SoC + Host Stack combination capable of DN assignment (i.e., register via Subsystem combination, not as an End Product), so their downstream customers retain the ability to Include their registration's DN.
consultant_answer: Showing 'Details' in the DN field doesn't indicate no DN exists -- it's just the new site's display quirk for unmodified-design reuse registrations. If you Include two or more existing QDID/DNs together, the site does assign a real Design Number (prefixed 'Q30', meaning QPRDv3.0) to the combined design, visible via the Details link, and it has exactly the same legal effect as an older-style QDID -- other companies can Include it in their own registrations just like before. (If you Include only one QDID/DN, no DN gets assigned, same as before.) One important caveat: this only works because you happened to Include both a Controller Subsystem and a Host Subsystem -- if your SoC were instead registered as a complete End Product, no DN would be assigned at all. Since you sell modules to set-makers, I'd recommend continuing to choose SoC + Host Stack combinations that can receive a DN, for your downstream customers' benefit.
decision_logic: When a registration combining existing QDID/DNs without modification shows 'Details' or 'Default' in the DN field, check whether two or more QDID/DNs were Included -- if so, a genuine Q30-prefixed DN with full legal equivalence to a pre-2024 QDID has been assigned and is visible via the Details link; if only one QDID/DN was Included, no DN is assigned. Module/component sellers should register via Subsystem-combination paths (not as a complete End Product) to ensure their registration remains DN-eligible for downstream customers' benefit.
final_recommendation: When a customer is alarmed by a 'Details'/'Default' DN display after an unmodified-design-reuse registration, reassure them this is a cosmetic site-display quirk rather than a registration deficiency, and explain the underlying Q30-prefixed DN's full legal equivalence; for component/module sellers specifically, proactively recommend Subsystem-combination registration (rather than End Product registration) to preserve DN eligibility for downstream OEM customers.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer unaware of this display behavior might mistakenly conclude their registration failed to obtain a usable DN and either abandon a viable registration path or, conversely, a module seller who registers as an End Product without realizing it forfeits DN assignment could unintentionally limit their downstream customers' ability to Include their registration.
